How much does the NotebookLM API cost?
The only official one, the Gemini Notebook Enterprise API, needs Gemini Notebook for Enterprise licenses, which cost $9 per license per month after a 30-day trial, with a 15-license minimum. The Gemini API’s File Search charges for indexing and model tokens instead, and its storage is free.

title: Does Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) Have an API? Every Route, Compared (November 2026)
snippet:
Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) now has a developer API, the Gemini Notebook API: a Public Preview for personal Google accounts, at no charge during the preview. It only creates notebooks and adds sources: it generates no content of any kind (no audio or video overviews, reports, mind maps, quizzes or slide decks) and cannot answer questions about your sources. The Enterprise API makes only audio overviews, for licensed users at $9 per license per month (minimum 15). The Podcast API is deprecated. Unofficial libraries and hosted services use your own account, at your risk; AutoContent API is an independent alternative.

| Gemini Notebook API (Google, Public Preview) | Nothing generated: it only creates, lists and updates notebooks, and adds web pages, YouTube videos, plain text and Markdown as sources. The API has no method for audio or video overviews, reports, mind maps, quizzes, infographics, slide decks or questions. A remote MCP server gives the same notebook and source tools. | No charge during the Public Preview. title: notebooklm-py/docs/quota-limits.md at main · teng-lin/notebooklm-py
snippet:
A human-reference table of NotebookLM's **static, published plan limits** per tier — how many notebooks, sources, chats, and studio artifacts each subscription level allows.
**What this is NOT:** the newer unified compute meter. `GET_USER_SETTINGS` still carries only static plan limits, but an enabled account now receives live per-account percentages and reset timestamps from `ListQuotaSummary`. That meter is a separate system from the published per-feature limits in this document; see [ADR-0037](https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0037-live-usage-and-quota-api.md) for the live wire evidence and implemented API.

`(await client.settings.get_account_limits()).tier` (and the `tier` field in MCP/REST `server_info(include_account=True)`) returns the subscription tier as an **opaque integer** read from `GET_USER_SETTINGS` `limits[4]`. This table is what those integers *mean* in quota terms.
| `tier` int | Plan | Live-confirmed? |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | Standard / Free | ✅ yes (source limit 50 matches Google) |
| `2` | Pro | ✅ yes (source limit 300 matches Google) |
| `4` | Plus | decoded from the web pro-badge bundle |
| `3` | Ultra (20 TB) | decoded |
| `6` | Ultra (30 TB) | decoded |
| `5` | "Expanded" | decoded — aligns with the **Workspace "Expanded"** access level below (not a consumer plan, which is why it is absent from Google's consumer page) |

- **Deep Research is the only monthly quota**, and only at Standard/free (10/month) — a counterintuitive kink (Standard 10/month vs Plus 3/day) Google publishes on both consumer and Workspace pages.

title: NotebookLM API Options in 2026: Google Enterprise API, Free Libraries or a Hosted API
snippet:
If you want to automate NotebookLM on an ordinary free or paid Google account, there are three kinds of options:
1. **Google's Enterprise API**, if your organisation buys Enterprise licenses.
2. **Free open-source libraries and local MCP servers**, such as [notebooklm-py](https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py) and [gemini-notebook-mcp-cli](https://github.com/jacob-bd/gemini-notebook-mcp-cli), which you install and run on your own machine.
3. **A hosted API**, such as the [useapi.net NotebookLM API (Gemini Notebook API)](https://useapi.net/docs/api-gemini-notebook-v1), which runs on our servers with your own Google account, over REST and as a hosted [MCP server](https://useapi.net/docs/api-gemini-notebook-v1/mcp).

| | useapi.net | notebooklm-py | gemini-notebook-mcp-cli | Google Enterprise API |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted, nothing to install or run locally | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Hosted MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code | ✅ | ❌ (local only) | ❌ (local only) | ❌ |
| Works on free and paid consumer Google accounts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Sign-in without copying cookies; session kept fresh for you | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| REST API from any language | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Webhook when a job finishes | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Automatic load balancing across Google accounts | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Ready-to-import n8n templates | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Price | $15/month, every useapi.net API | Free | Free | Enterprise licenses |

A single **$15/month** subscription covers every API on useapi.net — one token, all services. You connect up to 3 of your own provider accounts per service, and useapi.net handles the REST API, load balancing, and polling.
[Pricing, crypto payment, and volume options](https://useapi.net/docs/subscription) — full refund within the first 14 days if you have fewer than 50 successful generations.
### Frequently asked questions
**Is there a free NotebookLM API?** Google offers no free API for regular accounts. Free open-source libraries exist and run on your own machine. The useapi.net API is $15/month, works on the free Google plan, and has a full refund within 14 days if you made fewer than 50 successful generations.

title: NotebookLM API Cost Comparison 2026: Prices, Plans & Value
snippet:
In 2026 Google [intro](https://ai-blog-ten-steel.vercel.app/posts/ai-generated-podcast-intro-outro-music-tutorial-2026)duced a tiered pricing structure that mirrors the industry shift toward usage‑based billing. The **Free tier** offers 5 M tokens and 2 GB of storage, while the **Pro** and **Enterprise** tiers scale down to $0.0045 and $0.0032 per 1,000 tokens respectively. These numbers are critical when you compare them against competitors like Anthropic’s Claude 2 (starting at $0.0065/1k tokens) and OpenAI’s GPT‑4 Turbo (starting at $0.0048/1k tokens).

## NotebookLM Pricing Tiers in 2026
| Tier | Monthly Token Allowance | Token Cost (per 1,000) | Storage Included | Additional Fees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | 5 M tokens | $0.00 (free) | 2 GB | $0.001 per GB egress |
| **Pro** | Up to 10 M tokens | $0.0045 | 10 GB | $0.001 per GB egress, $0.0005 per fine‑tune hour |
| **Enterprise** | Unlimited (custom caps) | $0.0032 | 100 GB + dedicated VPC | $0.0008 per GB egress, $0.0004 per fine‑tune hour, SLA‑based support [fees](https://ai-blog-ten-steel.vercel.app/posts/kaggle-api-cost-comparison-2026) |
**Key observations**
1. **Token discounts are steep** after the [free tier](https://ai-blog-ten-steel.vercel.app/posts/copilot-free-tier-limits-2026); moving from Pro to Enterprise saves **~28 % per token**.
2. **Storage is generous**—the Enterprise tier’s 100 GB is enough for most large‑scale notebook repositories.
3. **Egress fees** are modest but can become signifi[cant](https://ai-blog-ten-steel.vercel.app/posts/n8n-free-tier-limits-2026) for data‑heavy pipe[lines](https://ai-blog-ten-steel.vercel.app/posts/tutorial-ai-driven-ab-testing-email-subject-lines-2026) (e.g., exporting large PDFs).
For a typical SaaS product that processes **3 M tokens/month** with occasional spikes to 8 M, the Pro tier’s flat‑rate cost would be **$13.50** (8 M × $0.0045/1k) plus a negligible egress charge.

```markdown
| Tier | Tokens Included | Cost per 1k Tokens | Storage | Egress | Fine‑Tune Rate |
|------|----------------|--------------------|---------|--------|----------------|
| Free | 5 M | $0.00 | 2 GB | $0.001/GB | $0.0005/h |
| Pro | Up to 10 M | $0.0045 | 10 GB | $0.001/GB | $0.0005/h |
| Enterprise | Unlimited | $0.0032 | 100 GB | $0.0008/GB | $0.0004/h |
```

The Free tier grants **5 million input + output tokens per month**. This covers roughly 1,250,000 average‑length prompts (assuming 4 tokens per prompt) and includes 2 GB of storage for notebook assets.
